claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations and local chemical order.
Conventional first-principles approaches to multicomponent-alloy optimization have high computational demands.
Conventional CALPHAD and full-DFT methods are insufficiently accurate for fracture-property prediction.
A transformer model can accurately predict Young's modulus for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
A transformer model can accurately predict yield strength for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
A transformer model can accurately predict fracture toughness for hierarchical-heterostructured HfNbTiVAl10.
Descriptors derived from binary phase diagrams can encode phase stability in high-entropy alloys.
The proposed expandable descriptors capture atomic clustering and local chemical ordering.
DFT-derived pair-interaction features can be combined with phase-diagram descriptors to predict the specified tensile and fracture properties.
Transformer self-attention can capture intricate elemental interactions relevant to mechanical-property prediction in high-entropy alloys.
The hierarchical heterostructure redistributes bonding strengths.
Multilevel chemical fluctuations and local ordering influence dislocation dynamics in HfNbTiVAl10.
Representing clustering, ordering, and phase stability through self-attention is sufficient to map the hierarchical heterostructure to Young's modulus, yield strength, and toughness.
The integrated transformer model will be more accurate than CALPHAD and full-DFT methods.
Machine-learning workflows can reduce discovery or prediction cost relative to computationally demanding traditional approaches.
The proposed model will reduce prediction time by 100 to 1000 times.
The proposed model will reduce prediction error by 20% to 30% relative to traditional methods.
The model will lose reliability when microstructures, processing conditions, or compositions lie substantially outside its training domain.
The magnitude of the accuracy and efficiency gains depends on the representativeness of the training data.
